cleanIntro: A modern bolt gun with an honest three-step strip: safety on, magazine out, bolt back and out past the bolt stop. Springfield then publishes what most makers will not — how to take the bolt itself apart — and where the two stock screws go back to, at a stated torque.

steps.title: Glasses on, muzzle safe, safety to S
steps.action: Eye protection first, muzzle somewhere harmless, finger off the trigger, and the safety selector to 'S'. The book puts these in that order before the magazine even comes out.
steps.aside: POINT GUN IN SAFE DIRECTION WHILE KEEPING FINGER OFF THE TRIGGER.
steps.quote: Always use proper eye protection when cleaning firearms.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIPPING (printed p.26, per Figure 26-1 on the page)

steps.title: Magazine out and the rifle proved unloaded
steps.action: Drop the magazine and unload the rifle, then check the chamber by eye and by finger. This rifle fires with the magazine out if a round is chambered, which is exactly what the book's capitalised warning is about.
steps.aside: ALWAYS REMEMBER THE FIREARM IS ABLE TO FIRE WITH OR WITHOUT THE MAGAZINE IN PLACE.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIPPING (printed p.26, per Figure 26-1 on the page)

steps.title: Adjustable cheek piece off first, if the rifle has one
steps.action: If yours has an adjustable cheek piece, take it off before the bolt comes back — on an adjustable stock the riser sits in the bolt's path and you will be levering the bolt past it otherwise.
steps.quote: Remove the cheek piece if rifle is equipped with an adjustable cheek piece (See Know Your Firearm Section).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIPPING (printed p.26, per Figure 26-1 on the page)

steps.title: Bolt fully back, then press the REAR of the bolt stop
steps.action: Draw the bolt to its rearmost position and press the rear surface of the bolt stop, then pull the bolt straight out to the rear. Pressing the front of the stop does nothing; it is the rear face that releases.
steps.aside: The rifle is now field stripped for routine cleaning.
steps.quote: Depress the rear surface of the bolt stop and remove the bolt rearward (Figure 261).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIPPING (printed p.26, per Figure 26-1 on the page)

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber to the muzzle, ejection port down
steps.action: Lay the barrelled action horizontally with the ejection port facing DOWN so solvent runs out rather than into the action, and always clean from the chamber end toward the muzzle. Push the brush fully out of the muzzle before pulling back — reversing a brush mid-bore is how one jams.
steps.aside: You cannot change direction of the brush when brush is in the bore as this can jam the brush in the bore.
steps.quote: NOTE: Barrel should lay horizontally with the ejection port facing downward during cleaning. Always clean the barrel from the chamber to the muzzle.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — CLEANING THE BARREL (PDF p.34; this edition prints no page folios)

steps.title: Patch until clean, then oil, then take the oil back out
steps.action: Solvent-soaked jag and patch through, repeating with a fresh patch each time until nothing shows, then one oiled patch and one dry patch behind it. The dry patch matters: oil left standing in a bore is an obstruction and a fouling magnet.
steps.aside: Push a clean dry patch through the barrel to remove excess lubricant.
steps.quote: Repeat using a new patch each time, until the patch no longer shows fouling present.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — CLEANING THE BARREL (PDF p.34; this edition prints no page folios)

steps.title: Bolt raceways and lug faces get the oil — three points, no more
steps.action: Oil goes in three places on this rifle: the bolt body, the bolt ways inside the receiver, and the rear faces of the bolt locking lugs. Nothing else needs it, and grease belongs nowhere near the firing pin or the inside of the bolt body.
steps.aside: NOTE: Do not use grease in the bore of the bolt body or on the firing pin or spring.
steps.quote: Inside of the receiver in the bolt ways (Figure 32-2), and rear faces of the bolt locking lugs (Figure 32-3).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — LUBRICATION POINTS (printed p.32, per Figures 32-1 to 32-3)

deepSteps.title: Shroud compressed 1/8", handle pressed in — that is the catch
deepSteps.action: With the bolt out of the rifle, push the shroud forward about an eighth of an inch and hold it there while you press the bolt handle inward, then release the shroud. That sequence is what unlocks the assembly; doing it in the other order simply does nothing.
deepSteps.quote: Compress the shroud towards the front of the bolt 1/8” and while maintaining pressure, Press the handle inward, (Figure 29-1) then release the pressure on the shroud (Figure 29-2).
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — BOLT DISASSEMBLY (printed p.29, per Figures 29-1 to 29-4)

deepSteps.title: Firing pin assembly out, then the bolt handle off the body
deepSteps.action: The firing pin assembly lifts out as a unit, and the bolt handle then comes off the bolt body. That is the end of it — Springfield says no further disassembly is required, and the firing pin assembly is not opened.
deepSteps.aside: No further disassembly is required. Bolt disassembly is now complete.
deepSteps.quote: The firing pin assembly can now be removed (Figure 29-3).
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — BOLT DISASSEMBLY (printed p.29, per Figures 29-1 to 29-4)

deepSteps.title: Everything solvent-cleaned, rinsed, dried and INSPECTED
deepSteps.action: Clean the parts with a quality powder solvent, rinse, dry and look at them properly before anything goes back — this is the one moment you can see the firing pin tip and the shroud. Lubricate the bolt lightly and wipe the excess away; no grease in the bolt body's bore.
deepSteps.quote: Clean all parts with a quality powder solvent, rinse, dry and inspect. Lightly lubricate the bolt, wipe away any excess lubricant.
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — BOLT DISASSEMBLY (printed p.29, per Figures 29-1 to 29-4)

deepSteps.title: Receiver flushed with the stock off — and the screws go back in order
deepSteps.action: For a proper receiver clean, take the two stock screws out with a 3/16 hex, lift the stock away, flush the inside of the receiver with an aerosol action cleaner and let it dry. Going back: the LONGER screw is the rear one, the FORWARD screw is tightened first, and neither goes past 65 in-lbs. Getting that order or that torque wrong is how a bedded action loses its zero.
deepSteps.aside: NOTE: Tighten the forward screw first followed by the rear. Do not exceed 65in lbs.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the 2 stock screws with a 3/16 Hex drive (Figure 27-1).
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — CLEANING THE RECEIVER (printed p.27, per Figure 27-1 on the page)

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Correct-caliber brush, solvent, chamber to muzzle, port facing down
Fresh patch each pass until nothing shows
One oiled patch, then one dry patch to take the excess back out

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Solvent on the body, lugs and bolt face; rinse, dry and inspect
Light oil on the body and the rear lug faces only
⛔ No grease in the bolt body bore, on the firing pin or on its spring

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & ACTION
tasks: Bolt ways wiped and lightly oiled
Aerosol action cleaner inside the receiver with the stock off, then dry
Thin coat of oil on the outside of barrel and action with a soft cloth

cleaning.name: STOCK SCREWS
tasks: 3/16 hex; the longer screw is the rear one
Forward screw tightened first, then the rear, and never past 65 in-lbs

reassembly: Bolt handle back onto the bolt body, then the firing pin assembly into the body.
Shroud compressed forward while the handle seats, then released to lock the assembly together.
Bolt into the receiver raceways and run forward; check it locks and unlocks freely.
Cheek piece back on if it was removed.
If the stock was off: action into the stock, FORWARD screw tightened first, then the rear (the longer of the two), neither past 65 in-lbs.
Function test before any live ammunition.
fncheck: Rifle empty, magazine out, muzzle safe. Work the bolt several times and feel it run and lock without drag. With the safety at 'S' the trigger must not release the striker; move it off and the rifle should function normally. If the bolt binds or the safety behaves inconsistently, stop and call Springfield rather than shooting it.
